title: AI_browser
summary:
An AI browser is a web browser with integrated artificial intelligence capabilities, such as automatically summarizing web page content or answering questions about it. A more specialized type is an agentic browser, based on the concept of agentic AI, which can take actions such as navigating webpages or filling out forms on behalf of the user.

Key AI browsers include Comet by Perplexity AI, a Chromium-based AI-powered web browser released for Microsoft Windows and macOS on July 9, 2025, integrated with Perplexity's AI-assisted search engine. ChatGPT Atlas by OpenAI is another AI browser based on Chromium, currently only available on macOS, integrating ChatGPT directly into the browsing interface via a sidebar assistant that can summarize page content, compare products, and analyze information. Dia by The Browser Company replaced the Arc browser after the company shifted all focus to developing its new AI browser in 2025.

The designation of AI browser also includes established browsers that later added non-agentic AI features, such as Microsoft Edge with the Copilot chatbot, Google Chrome with the Gemini chatbot, and Firefox with multiple chatbot providers including ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Gemini, and Le Chat. Several agentic browsers emerged in 2025, including ChatGPT Atlas, Comet, and Dia.

AI browsers have been noted to be susceptible to prompt injection attacks, in which the content of websites can be used to hijack the control of the browser. The United Kingdom national cyber security centre and Gartner consider them to be too risky for adoption by most organisations due to this vulnerability.
